tiles.title: What's the evaluate tab doing here?

text:
You already started evaluating in the "investigating" tab, and now all the tabs are out of order. What gives?!

Engineering and science don't follow totally clear, clean steps.

They're more like a messy pathway to discovery and invention!

You made your arm bionic!!! Before we figure out what to design next, we need to reflect and evaluate the current situation!

Did anything work really well?

Did you have to change anything in your hardware (the bionic arm) or your software (the Dataflow program) for your bionic arm to work?

tiles.title: Did anything work really well from the start? What challenges did you have?
What did you change, and why?
Is it working now? What do you think about it?

text:
Demo at your table

One or two group members will demonstrate the latest prototype.

You all worked on the same physical prototype. Choose whose program you will use to showcase it.

Make sure you explain:

  1. Who you are designing for
  2. What was your decision about where to connect the electrodes, and why
  3. Your Dataflow program. At this point, some programs might already be starting to look different from each other!

Make sure you take notes, and remind the people visiting to leave their comments!

Walking around the class

The rest of your group: Walk around the class and look at other people's prototypes.

Ask them questions, and give them constructive feedback! Make sure it's something new - not what you wrote last time!

  • What did they do that you didn't think of?
  • What could be improved in their program?
  • What problems do you think their user might face when using the arm or program they designed?
  • Does their design seem like it would help the person they are designing for? If not, what could be changed?
  • How did your group solve a problem that they might also be facing?
